root_cause.text: The GFS2 mount/read-write transition error paths had incomplete cleanup logic, so failures in gfs2_fill_super() and gfs2_make_fs_rw() after successful resource initialization left created kthreads and the quota bitmap allocated without corresponding teardown.
root_cause.evidence: The patch moves gfs2_destroy_threads() to the shared fail_per_node label because “the fail_per_node label doesn't call gfs2_destroy_threads()” after init_threads() succeeds, and adds gfs2_quota_cleanup(sdp) when gfs2_quota_init() succeeded but gfs2_withdrawn(sdp) caused gfs2_make_fs_rw() to fail, matching the CVE’s two reported leaks.

intent_record.intent_summary: Avoid destroying GFS2 threads prematurely on read-write setup failure and defer cleanup to the common failure path.
intent_record.what: In the error-handling block after attempting to make the filesystem read-write in gfs2_fill_super(), the call to gfs2_destroy_threads(sdp) was removed, while gfs2_freeze_unlock(sdp), fs_err(...), and the jump to fail_per_node remain unchanged.
intent_record.how: At runtime, when this read-write transition fails, the function no longer destroys GFS2 threads at that point and instead relies on the subsequent failure path reached via fail_per_node for cleanup. This prevents premature or duplicate thread teardown during error handling.

intent_record.intent_summary: Destroy GFS2 threads during gfs2_fill_super() rollback at fail_per_node to properly clean up resources on mount failure.
intent_record.what: A call to gfs2_destroy_threads(sdp); was added in the error-handling path of gfs2_fill_super(), specifically after init_per_node(sdp, UNDO); at the fail_per_node label and before control continues to fail_inodes.
intent_record.how: When gfs2_fill_super() fails after per-node initialization has begun, the cleanup path now explicitly destroys previously created GFS2 threads before continuing inode and superblock teardown, preventing leftover threads from surviving a mount failure and ensuring resources are released in the correct rollback sequence.

intent_record.intent_summary: Clean up quota initialization when a withdrawn filesystem forces `gfs2_make_fs_rw()` to fail with `-EIO`.
intent_record.what: A brace-wrapped conditional block was added around the existing `if (!error && gfs2_withdrawn(sdp))` check, and within that block a new call to `gfs2_quota_cleanup(sdp);` was inserted before setting `error = -EIO`.
intent_record.how: If quota initialization succeeds but the filesystem is already withdrawn, the function now cleans up quota state before returning an I/O error, preventing leftover initialized quota resources from persisting on this failure path.

consistency_review.core_intent: Fix cleanup behavior on gfs2 read-write mount/setup failure paths so resources and threads are handled consistently when the filesystem withdraws or setup returns -EIO.

relevance_review.reason: The changes directly target the incomplete cleanup in GFS2 mount/read-write failure paths by fixing thread teardown handling and adding quota cleanup when gfs2_make_fs_rw() fails with -EIO, matching the stated root cause.

The change directly addresses the incomplete cleanup in gfs2_fill_super() error handling by destroying created GFS2 threads during rollback after partial initialization, matching the root cause of leaked resources on mount failure.

candidates.rationale: This allocates/initializes quota state, but the surrounding pre-fix logic could overwrite success with -EIO on withdrawal and return without corresponding quota cleanup, directly matching the leaked quota bitmap root cause.
This converts a post-initialization withdrawn state into an error after quota initialization succeeded, triggering the failure path that lacked quota teardown and thus exposed the cleanup bug.
This sends gfs2_fill_super() into the rollback path where pre-fix code did not destroy the already created GFS2 threads, making the missing cleanup in fail_per_node observable.
The fail_per_node rollback only undid per-node state before the fix; the absence of thread destruction around this rollback is the essence of the incomplete cleanup on mount failure.

This pre-fix direct destruction in the read-write setup error branch reflects the inconsistent cleanup design called out by the fix; it handled one path locally while the common rollback path lacked proper cleanup, contributing to incorrect resource/thread teardown behavior.

vuln_statements.explanation: This statement initializes quota resources during the read-write transition. If a later withdrawn-state check forces failure, the pre-fix error path returned without corresponding quota cleanup, causing the leaked quota bitmap described in the root cause.

This statement converts a withdrawn filesystem condition into an error after quota initialization may already have succeeded. In the pre-fix logic, that error path did not tear down the quota state, making this assignment the trigger for the incomplete cleanup.

This transfers control to the common rollback path in gfs2_fill_super(). Before the fix, that rollback undid per-node state but did not destroy already created GFS2 threads, so this jump exposed the incomplete cleanup causing thread leakage on mount failure.

bic_trace_step.reason: The function body is sufficient because it shows the full mount success path and all error unwind labels. The vulnerable construct is present in the error path after the filesystem is made read-write. Specifically, after `gfs2_statfs_init(sdp)` succeeds and `gfs2_freeze_lock(sdp, &freeze_gh, 0)` succeeds, the code does `if (!sb_rdonly(sb)) error = gfs2_make_fs_rw(sdp);` at lines 1203-1204, then on failure it executes `goto fail_per_node;` at lines 1207-1209. Given the stated root cause, this means a failure in `gfs2_make_fs_rw()` after successful resource initialization can leak created kthreads / quota bitmap because the error path jumps directly to `fail_per_node` without that cleanup. bic_trace_step.reason: The snippet is sufficient because it contains the full mount path in `fill_super()` and the thread setup/teardown logic in `init_threads()`, which is exactly where the described cleanup bug would appear. The vulnerable construct is present: `fill_super()` starts background threads via `error = init_threads(sdp, DO);` and then, for read-write mounts, calls `error = gfs2_make_fs_rw(sdp); if (error) ... goto fail_threads;`. On that failure path, cleanup only does `init_threads(sdp, UNDO);`, `init_per_node(sdp, UNDO);`, `init_inodes(sdp, UNDO);`, `init_journal(sdp, UNDO);`, etc. There is no cleanup of any quota bitmap or other resource allocated by `gfs2_make_fs_rw()` itself before unwinding. This matches the root cause that failures in the read-write transition after successful initialization could leak resources. The code also shows the incomplete teardown pattern for `gfs2_fill_super()`-side resources: once `init_threads()` has succeeded, only `fail_threads:` stops the three threads (`kthread_stop(sdp->sd_inoded_process);`, `kthread_stop(sdp->sd_quotad_process);`, `kthread_stop(sdp->sd_logd_process);`), but there is no evidence of additional cleanup for resources created after that point by `gfs2_make_fs_rw()`. Since the fix would require explicit cleanup of those RW-transition allocations and/or more complete error-path teardown, and such handling is absent from this version, `has_bug=true` and `is_fixed=false`.
